questions.explanation: Three major types of soils are found in Bihar— (i) Piedmont swamp soil, found in the north-western part of West Champaran district. (ii) Terai soil, found in the northern part of the state along the Nepal border. (iii) Gangetic alluvial soil—the plains of Bihar are covered with Gangetic alluvium (both new and old).

questions.q: Most of the area of Bihar is covered with -

options.E: None of the above/Above more than one

questions.explanation: Most of Bihar is covered with alluvial (Kachhari) soil.

questions.q: Which one of the following parts of Bihar is geologically older in age relatively?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Kharagpur Hills consist of Pre-Cambrian/Proterozoic rocks of the Munger–Rajgir range, whereas the Rohtas Plateau belongs to the Vindhyan sequence; the North-Western Hills are a part of the Shivalik Himalaya (Upper Tertiary to Early Quaternary), and the North Ganga Plain is the newest.

questions.q: The geographical structure of Bihar is made up of rock systems. Match the rock systems with their descriptions— A. Dharwar rock system 1. Formed by rapid deposition of sediments by Himalayan and Peninsular rivers B. Vindhyan rock system 2. Can be found in West Champaran district C. Quaternary rock system 3. A part of the oldest Archean rock system D. Tertiary rock system 4. Sandstone, limestone, dolomite, quartzite and shale are the main components of this rock system Use the code given below and choose the correct answer. A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Dharwar rock system — A part of the oldest Archean rock system Vindhyan rock system — Sandstone, limestone, dolomite, quartzite and shale are the main components of the rock system Quaternary rock system — Formed by rapid deposition of sediments by Himalayan and Peninsular rivers Tertiary rock system — Can be found in West Champaran district

questions.q: Which of the following districts does not have a Dharwar geological structure?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Bihar, districts with Dharwar stratigraphic structure lie in south-eastern Bihar. These include Munger, Nawada and Jamui, whereas Rohtas is a part of south-western Bihar. Vindhyan sequence rocks are found in this region. In Bihar, Vindhyan sequence rocks occur in the Kaimur region and the Son river valley (Rohtas).

questions.q: Which of the following physiographic divisions of Bihar does not share its boundary with Jharkhand?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The geomorphological division “Mithila Plain” of Bihar does not share its boundary with Jharkhand, whereas the Ganga– Son Divide, Anga Plain and Magadha Plain do share a boundary with Jharkhand.

questions.q: The percentage of land area of old Bihar that forms the State of Jharkhand is –
questions.explanation: Before the formation of Jharkhand, the total area of undivided Bihar was 173,877 sq. km. Out of this, 79,714 sq. km. area was used for the formation of the state of Jharkhand on 15 November, 2000. Hence, Jharkhand was formed by taking about 45.84% of the land of old Bihar; therefore, the nearest option (b) is correct. At present, the total area of Bihar is 94,163 sq. km.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the various geographical aspects of Bihar – I. Agriculture contributes nearly 67 per cent to Bihar's domestic product. II. Silk industry in Bihar provides self-employment to over 1,50,000 people III. About 47 lakh acres of land in Bihar get flooded every year, while 10 lakh acres remain permanently waterlogged. IV. 85 to 90 percent of Bihar's rural households own less than 5 acres of land each. Which of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation: At the time of the question, option (c) was the correct answer. In 2022–23 (provisional) and 2023–24 (quick estimate), the share of agriculture, forestry and fishing in Bihar’s gross state value added was 20.2 percent and 19.5 percent respectively. In 2024–25 (up to January 2025), the estimated number of persons employed in Bihar’s silk sector was 0.24 lakh. In 2023, about 2.914 million hectares area in Bihar was affected by floods.

questions.q: Which soil is mostly found in Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga and Champaran districts?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Darbhanga and Muzaffarpur districts, new alluvial soil (Khadar) is found. New alluvial soil (Khadar) is formed due to the deposition of debris/silt brought every year by the flood water of rivers. In East Champaran and West Champaran districts of Bihar, along with new alluvial soil (Khadar), Terai soil and Balsundari soil are also found.

questions.q: Kaimur Plateau is famous for –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Kaimur Plateau is famous for limestone. The Kaimur Plateau is located in Rohtas and Kaimur districts. This plateau is made up of shale, limestone and sandstone. On the basis of the limestone of this plateau, there is a cement industry at Banjari.

questions.q: North Bihar is famous for –
questions.explanation: 73.63 percent of the area of North Bihar is vulnerable to floods. Due to floods every year in this region, crops and public life get disrupted.

questions.q: Which of the following cities is located in the easternmost part of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Katihar is situated in the easternmost part of Bihar. To the south of Katihar lie Bhagalpur and Sahibganj district of Jharkhand; to the east lies Malda district of West Bengal; to the north lies Dinajpur district; and to the north and west lies Purnia.

questions.q: Brahmayoni Hill is located in which district of Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Brahmayoni Hill is a sacred hill located in Gaya district of Bihar. It is mentioned in the Mahabharata, Buddhist inscriptions, etc. Gaya district is situated on the bank of the Phalgu River.

questions.q: Which city of Bihar is surrounded by five hills?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Rajgir city of Bihar is surrounded by five hills, which is also mentioned in various texts including the Mahabharata. The hills of Rajgir are world-famous. The names of these five hills are Vipulagiri (Vipulachal), Ratnagiri, Udaygiri, Swarnagiri and Vaibhavgiri (Vaibhargiri). Gaya is surrounded on three sides by small rocky hills, named—Mangala-Gauri, Shring Sthan, Ramshila and Brahmayoni.

questions.q: The number of Indian states touching the boundary of Bihar is –
questions.explanation: At the time of the question, undivided Bihar shared its boundary with four states (Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, and West Bengal). After the bifurcation on 15 November 2000, the Indian states touching Bihar’s boundary are Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, and Jharkhand.

questions.q: Which of the following districts of Bihar does not share border with Nepal?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Bihar shares an international boundary of 729 km with Nepal. Seven districts of Bihar share a boundary with Nepal— Sitamarhi, Kishanganj, Araria, Supaul, Madhubani, East Champaran, and West Champaran.

questions.q: After the formation of Jharkhand how many districts were left with Bihar? (Nearest figure)
questions.explanation: After the formation of Jharkhand, 37 districts remained in Bihar. Before the formation of Jharkhand, Bihar had 55 districts. Eighteen districts of Bihar went to the newly formed state of Jharkhand. At present, Bihar has 38 districts. The 38th district, “Arwal”, was created in August 2001 by bifurcating Jehanabad.

questions.q: By how many districts of Bihar was Patna district bounded till July 2018?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: At present, Patna district shares its boundary with 9 districts, namely—Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Samastipur, Begusarai, Lakhisarai, Nalanda, Jehanabad, and Arwal.

questions.q: Which of the following districts of Bihar transferred some of its areas to West Bengal?
questions.explanation: During the reorganization of states in 1956, most parts of Purulia located in the then Manbhum district of undivided Bihar (except Patamda police station) and some parts of Purnia were transferred to West Bengal.

questions.q: Forests of Chhotanagpur are – (i) Evergreen (ii) Deciduous (iii) Savanna (iv) Thorny Select your answer out of the following codes –

options.A: i and ii both are true
options.C: ii and iii both are true

questions.explanation: The forests of the Chhotanagpur region mainly consist of deciduous vegetation, in which mahua, khair, semal, shisham, mango, and banyan are prominent. Along with this, savannatype forests are also found here. The presence of scattered trees in grassland (scrub) areas is a characteristic feature of savanna-type forests.

questions.q: The expansion of forest in Bihar is on the area of:
questions.explanation: According to the State of Forest Report (SFR), 1993, Bihar had forests over a total area of 26.587 lakh hectares. As per the India State of Forest Report (ISFR), 2023, Bihar has forest cover over an area of 7,532.45 sq km, which is 8% of the total geographical area.
questions.note: ⚠ No officially verified answer for this question. Per the 1993 State of Forest Report (contemporaneous with this question), Bihar's forest area was about 26.6 lakh hectares — closest to option (a) 28 lakh hectares (no exact match).

questions.q: The percent of the total geographical area of Bihar covered by forests is-
questions.explanation: During the period of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. According to the India State of Forest Report (ISFR), 2023, forest cover in Bihar is 8% (7,532.45 sq km) and tree cover is 2.52% (2,370.21 sq km) of the total geographical area (94,163 sq km). Thus, as per the updated status, the total forest cover and tree cover together account for 10.52% (9,902.66 sq km) of the state’s area.

questions.q: What is the percentage of all types of forest area to the total geographical area of Bihar State?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the India State of Forest Report, 2019, the forest area in Bihar was 7.84 percent of the total geographical area. According to the India State of Forest Report, 2023, the forest area in Bihar is recorded at approximately 8 percent of the total geographical area.

questions.q: Among the following districts, which one has the larger area under dense deciduous forest cover?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: At the time of the question as well as at present, West Champaran has the largest area under dense deciduous forests. According to the India State of Forest Report, 2023, West Champaran has a total forest area of 908.23 square kilometers, of which 303.78 square kilometers are very dense forest, 527.25 square kilometres is moderately dense forest, and 77.20 square kilometres is open forest.

questions.q: With reference to the mineral production in Bihar, consider the following statements: 1. Rohtas has the highest deposit of pyrites. 2. Limestone is found in Kaimur (Bhabhua), Munger and Rohtas districts. 3. Gold deposits are found in Jamui district. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: All the statements given in the question are correct. Rohtas has the largest reserves of pyrite. Limestone is found in Kaimur (Bhabua), Munger and Rohtas districts. Gold reserves are found in Jamui district. Therefore, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.q: Coal Reserves in Bihar on January 1, 2003 is (in million tonnes) –
questions.explanation: On 1 January, 2003, the estimated coal reserve in Bihar was 16 crore tonnes (160 million tonnes). According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2023, the coal reserves in Bihar as of 1 April 2022 were 4437 million tonnes.

questions.q: The estimated coal reserves in Bihar are –
questions.explanation: After the formation of Jharkhand as a separate state from Bihar, Bihar’s natural resources declined significantly. According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2023, Bihar has coal reserves of 4437 million tonnes (as of 1 April, 2022). At the time of the question, the estimated coal reserves in Bihar were 16 crore tonnes.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are largely mined in Bihar? I. Coal II. Iron III. Manganese IV. Petroleum Choose the correct answer from the following :
questions.explanation: During the relevant period, coal, iron ore and manganese— all three—were found. Petroleum was not found here. Therefore, in the context of undivided Bihar during that period, the correct answer was option (c). According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2023, minerals produced in Bihar include—coal, mica, quartz/silica sand, quartzite, talc/ soapstone/steatite, bauxite, china clay, feldspar, fire clay, gold, granite, iron ore (hematite + magnetite), lead-zinc, pyrite and limestone.

questions.q: Among the following pairs of mineral and district, which one is correctly matched?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2024, limestone is found in Kaimur (Bhabua), Munger and Rohtas districts; mica in Nawada district; quartzite in Lakhisarai, Munger and Nalanda districts; and lead-zinc in Banka and Rohtas districts.

questions.q: Iron ore is found in Jharkhand in the district –
questions.explanation: During the relevant period, in the context of undivided Bihar, the correct answer was option (d). In 1990, Singhbhum district was divided into East Singhbhum and West Singhbhum. According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2024, Bihar has iron ore reserves of 49439 thousand tonnes (hematite + magnetite).

questions.q: In India, Bihar is the largest producer of –
questions.explanation: During the relevant period, in undivided Bihar (including Jharkhand), mica had the highest production. According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2023, Bihar is a leading state in pyrite reserves. Andhra Pradesh holds the leading position in mica production.

questions.q: Which district of Bihar has mica deposits?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mica reserves are found in Nawada district of Bihar.

questions.q: Bihar produces .....% of pyrite of the whole India.
questions.explanation: According to the India Minerals Yearbook, 2023 In Bihar, 94 percent of India’s total pyrite reserves/resources are found. However, the word “produces” used in the question is technically incorrect. Therefore, the Bihar Public Service Commission deleted this question.
questions.note: ⚠ No officially verified answer for this question. Per the India Minerals Yearbook, Bihar accounts for about 94% of India's pyrite reserves; option (c) 90% is the closest of the given figures (the question was ultimately deleted by BPSC over the word 'produces' vs. 'reserves').

questions.q: In the production of the following in India, Bihar has a monopoly in –
questions.explanation: At the time of the question, Bihar had a monopoly in the production of pyrite in India. In Bihar, 94 percent of the country’s pyrite reserves are found.

questions.q: Gold is found in which district of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The entire recorded gold ore resource of Bihar is associated with Jamui district. Indian Minerals Year Book 2024, As of 1 April 2020, the total gold ore (primary) reserves/resources in Bihar are recorded as 222,884,860 tonnes.

questions.q: Gold is found in which of the following districts of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The entire recorded gold ore resource of Bihar is associated with Jamui district. Indian Minerals Year Book 2024, As of 1 April 2020, the total gold ore (primary) reserves/resources in Bihar are recorded as 222,884,860 tonnes.

questions.q: Which district of Bihar has the largest gold reserve?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.q: Best mica ore of the world is obtained from – 1. Dhanbad 2. Hazaribagh 3. Jharia 4. Kulti Select the correct answer from the following codes –
questions.explanation: At the time of the question, mica was obtained from Hazaribagh, Giridih, and Koderma. In Bihar, mica reserves are found in Nawada district.

questions.q: Palamau (Ranchi) is famous for which mineral?
questions.explanation: Indian Minerals Year Book 2024, Palamu district of Jharkhand, reserves of many minerals are found, the major ones being— (1) Bauxite (2) Dolomite (3) Fireclay (4) Graphite (5) Magnetite iron ore (6) Quartz/Silica sand (7) Talc/Steatite/Soapstone (8) Rock phosphate (9) Limestone (10) Feldspar (11) Coal (12) Granite (13) Gold
questions.note: ⚠ No officially verified answer for this question. Bauxite is the mineral most prominently associated with the Palamau/Palamu region among the choices given (the area actually has many minerals — bauxite, dolomite, coal, mica, etc.).

questions.q: What percentage of the total mineral production in the country is found in Bihar?
questions.explanation: In undivided Bihar, Bihar was rich in minerals. After bifurcation, most mineral-rich areas went to Jharkhand. Therefore, Bihar is no longer rich in minerals. At the time of the question, option (a) was the correct answer.

questions.q: In the production of crude copper in the country, Bihar ranks-
questions.explanation: In copper production, the position of the then Bihar was third. Hence, under the then prevailing conditions, the desired answer was option (a). At present, copper is not produced in Bihar. Indian Minerals Year Book 2024, In 2023–24 stood at the top in the production of copper concentrate.

questions.q: Which is the most important district of Jharkhand in iron ore production?
questions.explanation: The Singhbhum region of Jharkhand (East and West Singhbhum districts) holds the most important place in ironore production. The iron ore obtained from here is used in the Jamshedpur and Bokaro steel industries. 2023-24 (P), According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2024 Odisha is India’s top iron-ore producing state.

questions.q: Iron is obtained from which of the following minerals?
questions.explanation: Iron is mainly found in four types of ores—(i) Magnetite, (ii) Hematite, (iii) Limonite, and (iv) Siderite. Besides these, iron content is also found in taconite, chamosite, and pyrite. However, since the metal content in these is low, their economic importance is limited.

questions.q: Which of the following National Parks/Wildlife Sanctuaries are in Bihar? 1. Valmiki National Park 2. Dudhwa National Park 3. Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary 4. Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary Choose the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation: Among the given options, Valmiki National Park and Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary are in Bihar, whereas Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary is in Rajasthan and Dudhwa National Park is located in Uttar Pradesh. Valmiki National Park is located in West Champaran district. Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary is spread over 681.90 sq. km in Munger, Lakhisarai and Jamui districts.

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the given options, Valmiki National Park and Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary are in Bihar, whereas Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary is in Rajasthan and Dudhwa National Park is located in Uttar Pradesh. Valmiki National Park is located in West Champaran district. Bhimbandh Wildlife Sanctuary is spread over 681.90 sq. km in Munger, Lakhisarai and Jamui districts.

questions.q: Which of the following parks/sanctuaries come under the Project tiger in Bihar?
questions.explanation: Under the Government of India’s centrally sponsored scheme for tiger conservation, “Project Tiger,” the protected areas that are notified are considered Tiger Reserves. questions.q: At which place in Bihar, North India's first bird ringing station has been recently opened?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Bhagalpur (Bihar), India’s fourth “Bird Ringing and Monitoring Station” has been opened. questions.q: In which district of Bihar is the Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary located?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary is located in Bhagalpur district of the state of Bihar.

questions.q: Which of the following in Bihar started the Vulture Conservation Plan?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Valmiki Tiger Reserve (VTR) of Bihar has started the Vulture Conservation Scheme.

questions.explanation: The Karmanasha River is a tributary of the Ganga River, and it originates from the Kaimur Hills in Kaimur district of Bihar. This river forms the boundary between Uttar Pradesh and Bihar and ultimately meets the Ganga River near Chausa in Buxar district.

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Anupam Lake is located in Kaimur (Bihar). This lake lies within the boundary of the Kaimur Wildlife Sanctuary. options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: As per the question, among the given options, irrigation in Bihar is done through the Triveni Canal. This canal is related to the Gandak Irrigation Project. It is located in West Champaran district.

questions.explanation: The Karmanasa, Gandak and Ghaghara rivers determine the boundary line between Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. The Karmanasa merges into the Ganga near Chausa of Buxar, the Gandak near Pahleja Ghat (Saran district), and the Ghaghara near Revelganj (Saran district).

questions.explanation: The Gandak meets the Ganga near Pahleja Ghat (Saran district), the Ghaghara near Revelganj (Saran district), the Son near Maner, and the Punpun near a place called Fatuha.

questions.q: Which is the unique festival of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja is the most important festival of Bihar, and it is called the Mahaparv of Bihar. It is observed on the sixth day of the bright fortnight of the Kartik month, exactly six days after Diwali. On this festival, Surya Dev (Sun God) and Chhathi Maiya are worshipped, and Arghya is offered—first at sunset and the second at sunrise. Diwali, also called the festival of lights, is a major Hindu festival celebrated on the new moon day of the Kartik month. Vishu is the traditional New Year festival of Kerala. It is celebrated on the first day of the Malayalam month Medam and is considered a symbol of good luck for the coming year. Vinayak Chaturthi is celebrated by Hindus across India, including Maharashtra, on the Shukla Chaturthi of the month of Bhadrapada on the occasion of Lord Vinayak’s (Ganesha’s) birth.

questions.q: Which community was categorized as Scheduled Caste (SC) by a 2015 Bihar government notification which was quashed in july, 2024 by the Supreme Court, ruling that states cannot make changes to the SC list published under Article 341 of the Constitution ?
questions.explanation: In its 2015 notification, the Bihar Government classified the Tanti-Tantwa community, earlier included in the Extremely Backward Class category, as a Scheduled Caste (SC). This was set aside by the Supreme Court in July, 2015. The Supreme Court held that states do not have the power to modify the SC list published under Article 341 of the Constitution. Under Article 341, the list of Scheduled Castes for the states is issued by the President through a Constitutional Order, and any amendment can be made only by Parliament through legislation.
